correctness.rationale: For each positive modulus, the dyadic triangular map has exactly two preimages per residue over its 2-adic component by the opposite-parity factorization. For every odd prime power, the discriminant substitution is a bijection; a complete valuation-and-unit-square analysis supplies every root count (including zero and all even valuations). CRT yields all global fibers. Counting local nonzero-square discriminants gives the k-th moment formula for every integer k>=1, including k=1 and k=2; the independent zero-product count confirms the second moment. The prime-power square-residue count and dyadic surjectivity give both asserted saturations. Reproducible exact enumeration verified all fibers/supports/collisions for m<=1000 and k<=6 for m<=299; these finite tests do not prove the theorem.

originality.rationale: Ulness 2022 Theorem 5 gives the qualitative condition 1+8t square modulo m and Theorems 1/8 discuss periodic and dyadic behavior. His explicitly numbered Conjectures 1 and 2 state the quantitative prime-power and dyadic invariance laws rather than proving them. The new integrated theorem computes all fibers, every positive moment across arbitrary moduli, and thereby proves both conjectures. Classical quadratic-residue root enumeration is foundational input and is not claimed as new. Related 2019 triangular lacunary analysis treats geometry of Gauss-sum sequences, not fiber moment products. No searched published record was found with the full explicit claim; an independent literature audit remains outstanding.

value.rationale: The 2022 source explicitly introduces and motivates occupancy and multiplicity and states both the odd-prime-power and dyadic saturation laws as conjectures. This theorem proves both without bounding the exponent and supplies a complete exact distribution for every modulus, an infinite hierarchy of moment identities, and a simple multiplicative collision law. The full-distribution/moment invariant is motivated by the source rather than an arbitrary slice or a mere finite computation; its derivation uses classical machinery and no general theorem beyond this family is asserted.
